audit_findings.title: Post-anchor financing cost may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.188 million annual contractual interest on $1.4375 billion of 2031 Notes; 3.54 million potential shares versus 3.50 million shares of capped-call coverage
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-anchor notes increase recurring interest deducted from equity-level OE, while conversion and capped-call treatment affects fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $600.0 million in outstanding principal for the Convertible Senior Notes due in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing change is demonstrated: the FY2025 anchor predates the May 2026 notes, whose annual coupon is $7.188 million versus $1.500 million on the retired notes. That omission overstates OE. Conversely, the 45.610124 million share count appears to include the 3.54 million note shares even though principal must be settled in cash and capped calls cover approximately 3.50 million shares, potentially understating per-share value. Excluding 3.54 million shares mechanically raises base value from $167.05 to approximately $181.10 per share before correcting interest, so the inconsistent combined treatment is material.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate run-rate OE using the 2031 Notes' recurring after-tax cash interest and commitment fees, then rerun diluted shares using conversion-premium shares only when applicable and explicitly incorporate the capped calls and cash-principal settlement.

audit_findings.title: The latest balance sheet may include a post-anchor acquisition that the earnings numerator excludes
audit_findings.magnitude: $212.7 million cash purchase price net of acquired cash; $257.771 million total consideration; $25.338 million computed H1 2025 pro forma revenue increment
audit_findings.mechanism: The June bridge reflects acquisition consideration and financing, but FY2025 OE excludes FTR's post-acquisition earning power.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 2, 2026, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire the remaining equity interest of privately held company in which we currently hold a minority interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch: FTR closed on April 14, 2026, and the June balance sheet includes it, while the anchor remains FY2025. The $212.7 million cash price equals 2.8% of the $7.619 billion base equity value, and filed pro forma revenue exceeds reported H1 2025 revenue by $25.338 million. The corresponding recurring OE contribution cannot be isolated from the supplied pro forma net income because that measure is affected by the $25.048 million remeasurement gain and transaction adjustments. The missing earning power is therefore capable of materially affecting the valuation but is not yet quantified.
audit_findings.action: Add FTR's normalized, acquisition-accounting-neutral OE to the numerator from the closing date or restate both the numerator and bridge to a pre-FTR perimeter, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Historical growth may have been purchased but is forecast as costless organic growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $147.806 million filed acquisition cash outlays during 2023-2025; $214.291 million in H1 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition spending or its financing cost is required reinvestment if the forecast growth rates depend on purchased businesses.
audit_findings.evidence: A material portion of our historical growth has resulted from strategic acquisitions, and we expect to continue to identify and pursue strategic acquisitions with suitable candidates.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition outlays are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much of the modeled 7% or 9% growth requires recurring M&A. Tyler also produced meaningful recent growth excluding acquisition contributions, so it cannot be assumed that all forecast growth is purchased. Nevertheless, the outlays are large relative to the $379.7 million anchor OE and could materially overstate value if a normalized acquisition requirement is omitted.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic revenue and OE growth bridge excluding acquired businesses for each historical year, identify the acquisition spending required to sustain each scenario, and rerun with either normalized acquisition investment or independently supported organic growth rates.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized sales commissions may be missing from required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.768 million 2025 deferred-commission increase; computed base-value exposure approximately $381 million or $8.36 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring increase in deferred commissions is a cash reinvestment deduction from OE when net income already includes only commission amortization.
audit_findings.evidence: Sales commissions for initial contracts are deferred and then amortized commensurate with the recognition of associated revenue over a period of benefit that we have determined to be generally three to five years.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that deferred commissions rose from $56.799 million to $78.567 million while $21.881 million of amortization was already expensed. The supplied record does not establish whether the OE worksheet deducted the $21.768 million net asset build, so omission remains unresolved rather than proven. If omitted, it equals 5.7% of anchor OE and, using the model's base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, approximately $8.36 per share—large enough to be material.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE worksheet and reconcile commission cash additions, amortization, acquisition effects, and the deferred-commission balance change; deduct the net cash build once, without double-counting amortization, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The full cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Only genuinely surplus cash belongs in the equity bridge; operating, restricted, settlement-related, or committed cash supports OE or corresponding obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash in excess of that necessary for operating requirements is invested in short-term, highly liquid, income-producing investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge adds the full $970.035 million of June cash and short-term investments, equal to 12.7% of base equity value, but the filing does not quantify minimum operating liquidity, government-partner funds, restricted balances, or transaction commitments. The possible overstatement could therefore be material, but the record cannot establish the amount. The separate exclusion of $45.232 million of non-current investments does not resolve whether the included cash is surplus.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June cash accounts to restricted and custodial balances, government-partner settlements, committed uses, and documented minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor retains potentially nonrecurring contract-loss reserves
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.4 million pretax; approximately $16.5 million after tax using the filed 19.1% rate; computed base effect approximately $289 million or $6.34 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing demonstrably nonrecurring reserves would increase normalized anchor OE and its projected cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease of 9% in the PT segment operating income in 2025 is primarily due to loss reserves of approximately $10.7 million for two state contracts, primarily impacting lower revenue from professional services, as well as higher merchant fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 filing identifies $10.7 million of PT reserves and $9.7 million of ES exposure, but it does not prove they are nonrecurring or free of future cash costs. Even granting the entire $20.4 million as nonrecurring, the approximate after-tax adjustment is only 4.3% of the $379.7 million anchor. It would raise base value from $167.05 to about $173.39 per share and bull value from $183.89 to about $190.96, still far below the $364.03 market price; it therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm resolution and cash consequences of both contract exposures and examine prior-year loss frequency; normalize only the demonstrably nonrecurring portion, although no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated at the maximum supplied amount.
